notes: Cygnus OA-6, June 2016. Sensor workbook: cabin pressure 14.877 psia, steady; igniter on 60-68 s at about 190 W; downstream radiometers saw the flame from about 62 to 147 s. CO2 rise is the peak of a 10 s running mean at the avionics-bay sensor (0.6282% to 0.6449%); the O2 change stayed within sensor drift; Saffire-I had no CO sensor. Plume thermocouple peak 94.4 C. source: NASA PSI table PSI-100 (Saffire-III); flight from Spaceflight101 OA-7 report; Saffire-III sample 1 sensor workbook (NASA PSI); Saffire-III telemetry workbook (NASA PSI)
notes: Cygnus OA-7, 4 June 2017. Same sample as Saffire-I (94 x 40.6 cm) at a higher flow, 30 cm/s listed (anemometers read about 24.5 and 25.5 cm/s); thickness given as 0.33 cm. Sensor workbook: igniter on 60.0 to 68.0 s; radiometers saw flame from 63 to 422 s (about 359 s); cabin CO2 rose from 0.395% to 0.605% (about 2098 ppm, 1.57 mmHg, peak of a 10 s mean) and was still elevated when the record ended at 690 s; thermocouples in the sample peaked at 1,088 C and in the plume at 96 C. Saffire's pressure sensor read 14.46 psia while the Cygnus cabin sensors read 13.99 psia, a 0.47 psi disagreement left unresolved. The O2 sensor read 19.8% before ignition, low for cabin air (Saffire-I's read high, 22.3%), so O2 is uncertain. No CO sensor on Saffire-III. Telemetry also shows the cabin smoke detector responding (C-49)

source: NASA PSI table PSI-100 (Saffire-III); flight from Spaceflight101 OA-7 report; Saffire-III telemetry workbook (NASA PSI); pressure from Saffire-III sample 1 sensor workbook (NASA PSI)
notes: Cygnus OA-7, June 2017. Same sample as Saffire-I (94 x 40.6 cm) at 30 cm/s, opposed flow; thickness given as 0.33 cm. Burned first: igniter current seen at 8,383 s; radiometers 2 and 4 rose 6 to 12 mW/cm2 above baseline in only two 30 s samples (8,413 and 8,443 s), then nothing, so the opposed flame was small or brief (30 to 90 s seen). The 30 s sampling cannot say whether it went out or stayed too small to register. No O2, CO2 or CO channels in the telemetry. Pressure is Saffire's sensor during sample 1, about 4 minutes later (14.46 psia; the Cygnus sensors read 13.99 psia)
